FLAG_E.definition: FIRES if a paper reports that ACTIVATION quantisation (FP8 or INT8 activations, any scale granularity; W8A8, W4A8, FP8 activations with per-token or per-tensor scales; FP8 KV-cache counts as activation-side) changes the behavioural effect, success rate or direction of an activation-level intervention (steering/activation addition, noise injection, patching, ablation, SAE-latent editing) relative to higher-precision activations on the same or matched weights. PARTLY FIRED if the varied factor is weight-only (INT8/NF4/INT4/GPTQ/AWQ), or the outcome is internal only (vector cosine, probe accuracy), or numerics change intervention outcomes only via batch/kernel nondeterminism. ADJACENT if numerics or quantisation change outputs with no intervention (nondeterminism, FP8 outlier sensitivity, flips).
FLAG_E.summary: No verified full text isolates ACTIVATION quantisation and shows it changes the behavioural effect of an activation-level intervention at matched weights, so FLAG E does not FIRE. It is PARTLY FIRED three ways: (1) weight-only evidence (Steering Under Compression: bitsandbytes INT8/NF4, activations kept FP16/BF16; PRISM: NF4); (2) joint weight+activation 8-bit RTN quantisation breaks activation-patching circuit discovery (PAHQ; FP32 vs 8-bit, GPT-2-scale, circuit-recovery AUC); (3) two contemporaneous ICLR 2027 submissions report, at abstract level, that the SAME steering intervention changes its behavioural effect across precision/low-bit quantisation while output fidelity and direction similarity are preserved, without stating whether activations are quantised (OpenReview PDFs HTTP 403).

FLAG_E.consequence_for_wording: Claim E's 'deployment finding' must not be framed as new in its general form ('quantisation can change what a fixed activation intervention does although quality and direction similarity are preserved'): that is occupied (contemporaneous, abstract-level). Claim E may claim, dated and 'to our knowledge': the activation-vs-weight attribution (2x2 W8A8/W8A16/W16A8/W16A16 factorial on identical hook code), a per-token-scaled FP8 W8A8 production engine (not unscaled casting or RTN), content-free random nudges at matched per-position dose with CRN slots, a categorical test-checked algorithm-choice outcome, and per-token absmax/FP8-scale readouts. If the full texts of OR:8iTqrW1sxY or OR:h57duZqLOr show activation quantisation, Claim E becomes a replication in a new setting (content-free nudges, code algorithm choice).

FLAG_L.definition: FIRES if a paper (i) perturbs, steers, prompts against or fine-tunes a tuned model away from its default output, (ii) forecasts from the base model where it lands (identity or distribution, any granularity), and (iii) scores that forecast against a rival built from the tuned model itself (its own sampled tail, its own likelihood ranking of alternatives, or its pre-perturbation distribution). PARTLY FIRED if (i)+(ii) without (iii); or (ii)+(iii) retrospective rather than forecast; or token-level only with (i)-(iii). ADJACENT: candidate preservation under post-training without a perturbation (URIAL, Same Candidates, Sparse but Critical, crystallization), stylised accounts (power sharpening).
FLAG_L.summary: No paper forecasts, from the base model, which enumerated alternative a perturbed TUNED model lands on and scores that forecast against the tuned model's own sampled tail or likelihood ranking, so FLAG L does not FIRE. It is PARTLY FIRED by fine-tuning-perturbation work on reversion toward base behaviour: Re-Emergent Misalignment ((ii)+(iii) retrospective, sequence likelihoods: the instruct model suppresses what base and misaligned models share), Language Models Resist Alignment and Alignment Dynamics ((i)+(ii) at distribution/score level, no tuned rival), and the Gravitational Interpretation of Safety Reversion ((i)+(ii) prospective, direction toward base-descended helpful-only states, rival = matched geometric null). Token-level candidate preservation remains adjacent (URIAL, Sparse but Critical, Same Candidates). Rival-supporting evidence exists: jailbroken landings lie in the safe model's own top-10 (Weak-to-Strong), and an EM persona subspace extracted from the frozen tuned model forecasts where fine-tuning lands (Nadaf 2026).

FLAG_L.consequence_for_wording: Not a replication. The 92d A2 sentence is updated: reversion of fine-tune-perturbed tuned models toward base behaviour is reported at distribution/likelihood level (retrospective, or prospective against a geometric null), and candidate preservation is reported at token level; to our knowledge (dated search), no work commits in advance to an algorithm-level landing forecast from the base composition and scores it against the tuned model's own likelihood ranking (q_lik) and sampled tail (q_tail), including tail-empty events. 'First' is not licensed.
